730830401.text: We're back at Aaru Village again. Whoa! This place is still burning hot, just like how it was on our first visit.

730830402.text: Paimon wonders how Jeht and Tirzad are doing... Paimon's kinda concerned.

730830404.text: Yes, that's what Paimon thinks too, even if we're just speculating here.

730830405.text: The last expedition should have helped with their composure, or... should we say that they're growing up?

730830406.text: I'm not sure if we can call what Tirzad did "growing up"...

730830407.text: But Jeht said that he was like a tantrum-throwing kid...

730830412.text: Sorry for interrupting your conversation. I'm Kalantari, a student in the Akademiya. I seek traces of the past that remain on the earth.

730830413.text: Were you part of Tirzad Hindi's recent expedition in the desert?

730830415.text: It really is you! He mentioned both of you in the acknowledgments of his paper.

730830416.text: Paper? Oh yeah, he did say he would focus on writing his paper once he got back. So it's done already?

730830417.text: Yup, he locked himself in his room once he got back from the desert. The other researchers were worried that he was depressed from failing to obtain any results from his expedition.

730830418.text: After a few days, we started betting on whether he would eat or drink first when he finally came outside. But he suddenly charged out and submitted a paper to the Akademiya...

730830419.text: "The Golden Slumber: A Study on Governance in the Later Period of Al-Ahmar's Civilization and Stages of Survival."

730830420.text: It may sound a little rude, but I never expected Tirzad to be capable of writing such a groundbreaking paper.

730830409.text: Yes, we'll definitely meet Jeht again as long as we continue adventuring.

730830410.text: As for Tirzad... We can find him in the Akademiya. He calls himself an Indoorsology researcher, after all...

730830502.text: Huh? That voice sounds really familiar...

730830503.text: Kalantari, I didn't expect you to sneak all the way to Aaru Village. This old bag of bones is going to fall apart chasing after you, you know?

730830504.text: Oh, it's Mr. Soheil! Someone at your age should be reading through texts and records in the Akademiya. What are you doing all the way out here?

730830505.text: Hmph! What am I doing here? I'm here to stop you youngsters from running off into the desert, of course!

730830506.text: All of you have read quite a few papers, yet you can't keep your cool. Tirzad gains some success once, and you all go charging into the desert like mindless Fungi.

730830507.text: The sage is afraid you'll alert the matra and worried that you might damage the ruins, so I was sent to dissuade all of you.

730830508.text: All of us...? But I came alone, and I even specially applied for paid leave to keep it a secret from everyone else.

730830509.text: You did come here alone, but you're not the only one with the same idea. Do you know how many leave applications the sage received yesterday?

730830510.text: Forty-six! A total of forty-six applications! All of them from young students wanting to try their luck after reading that paper!

730830511.text: They gave all sorts of excuses. Helping a neighbor whose house caught on fire, a Fungi invasion turning their homes upside down, accidentally consuming spoiled curry... If only they used their creativity on writing papers!

730830513.text: Exactly! I mean, so many people supposedly applied for leave, but I didn't see a single one of them here in Aaru Village.

730830517.text: Of course you didn't! I have already convinced all forty-five of them to go back while on my way here. You're the last one.

730830518.text: Listen. Academic research never relies on luck. Tirzad may have produced a well-written paper, but we still haven't verified its credibility.

730830520.text: No buts! Having no prior experience is enough to get you lost in the desert. Even if you don't get lost, there's no guarantee you won't accidentally damage something within the ruins.

730830521.text: For the sake of your safety and the ruins', you must head back. If you refuse, I'll have to ask Hulwani from the Corps of Thirty to "escort" you back.

730830524.text: That's how a researcher of the Akademiya should act. Alright, off you go.

730830525.text: Huh? Mr. Soheil, you're not going back?

730830526.text: Of course not. I'll be staying here for some time to stop other rash researchers like you from entering the desert.

730830527.text: I'm not rash... I—I'm just in need of inspiration for my paper. *sigh* I thought I finally had my chance.

730830528.text: Goodbye, Traveler, and may we meet again. Safe travels.

730830515.text: And that's exactly why you should trust them. As they say, the absurdity of the truth often exceeds any researcher's imagination.

730830516.text: Besides, I haven't seen any other researcher here in Aaru Village, so there's a high chance they were all telling the truth.

730830601.text: Sorry, I was so busy with Kalantari that I didn't get to greet you. I'm Soheil from the Usaibia family, and a researcher from Vahumana.

730830602.text: Did he plan to hire you as his guide? In that case, I'm sorry for ruining your business.

730830603.text: But it may not be a bad thing. Tirzad's paper isn't very credible, so you might have ended up going all the way for nothing.

730830605.text: Oh? Why are you so sure? Wait. Are you... the ones mentioned in his acknowledgments...?

730830609.text: #Yes, that's us. We're the famed {NICKNAME} and Paimon, the travelers who went on an expedition with Tirzad!

730830610.text: Hmm, well. Being willing to support your employer is a good thing, I suppose. It shows that you value contracts just as the people of Liyue do. But you can't fool me.

730830611.text: I've been to the desert in my youth, but I have never once encountered places like the "Khemenu Temple" or "Khaj-Nisut" mentioned in that paper.

730830612.text: Besides that, the sandstorm at the top of the Mausoleum of King Deshret is still as I remember it from my youth. So, I suspect that Tirzad never entered the Mausoleum of King Deshret. He probably made it all up.

730830613.text: I'm fairly certain you took his Mora and got your stories straight so that when someone comes to check, his paper would seem more credible.

730830614.text: It might have been a good plan, but unfortunately, you ran into me.

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the location indicated by the stone slate

730830101.text: According to the stone slate, we've arrived at our destination!

730830102.text: It's just that... Paimon doesn't see any special devices, even though we're definitely inside the Mausoleum now. Have we gone the wrong way?

730830103.text: Should we have another look at the stone slate?

730830104.text: Huh? There's new writing on it... And three dots of light...

730830105.text: "The mortal plane is like a river between the underworld and Aaru. Mortals must not cross, must not probe, must not... Uh... Must not... Paimon doesn't know how to read that... or they shall descend into the underworld forever..."

730830106.text: "In order to ascend to Aaru, one must have a body like that of a vulture and soar above the underworld... Peck at three different organs in order to obtain the consent of Al-Ahmar, and fly across the river in the form of a falcon..."

730830108.text: Oh... "Must not covet." But what does that mean? This all sounds pretty important, but Paimon doesn't understand anything.

730830109.text: #Which one do you think is more important, {NICKNAME}?

730830111.text: In order to ascend to Aaru... Does that mean Aaru Village? But Paimon doesn't think Aaru Village existed back then... Anyway, shouldn't the opposite of the underworld be a really wonderful place?

730830116.text: Hmm, if we sum it all up, we must do something to the "organs" to open a new path that leads to "Aaru." Um... It all sounds kinda mysterious...

730830117.text: But speaking of "organs"... Paimon thinks we've heard that one somewhere.

730830113.text: Peck out three organ types... Do we really have to eat... organs...? That's scary...

730830115.text: Obtaining the consent of Al-Ahmar should refer to opening a new path.

730830201.text: Paimon has been thinking for a while now... This place feels really important... It's like Stormterror's Lair but in the desert!

730830202.text: Paimon wonders if bards sang about this place during King Deshret's reign... Let's get a closer look.

subQuests.subQuestName: Follow the stone slate's guidance and obtain full clearance

730830303.text: Well, according to the stone slate, we've obtained King Deshret's consent and reached "Aaru."

730830304.text: But this place doesn't seem very much like "Aaru." There's only this frighteningly huge device. Paimon feels that "Aaru" should be more... more...

730830310.text: Right, it doesn't look much different from the underworld we just passed through, and Paimon even sees a frighteningly huge device up ahead. Paimon feels that "Aaru" should be more... more...

730830701.text: Huh? Why are you still in Aaru Village? Are you thinking about trying to get something from me?

730830702.text: Just give up on that. I'm not Tirzad, Kalantari, or any of those other youngsters. I never try to take the easy way out.

730830703.text: Allow me to guide you to the right path. Start gaining knowledge now. Who knows, you might even make it into the Akademiya once you reach my age.

subQuests.subQuestName: Explore the area and find a way to activate the giant device

730830801.text: Please leave. Don't do anything unnecessary.

730831401.text: No, I refuse to escort you into the desert.

730831402.text: But the Mausoleum of King Deshret, which has remained the same for centuries, has undergone an unprecedented change. You saw it too just now, didn't you? I need to make a record...

730831403.text: It's also my first time seeing this change... However, the sage has prohibited researchers from entering the desert without his permission.

730831405.text: I—I'm not like those rash young researchers. I've dedicated years to studying in the Akademiya...

730831407.text: Hello, long time no see. Seems like you're having a nice time in Aaru Village!

730831408.text: Huh? What are the two of you doing here? I did say that I wouldn't pursue the matter, but you should stop going around deceiving people.

730831409.text: I'm getting old, so my time is way more precious than yours. Besides, I have more important business to attend to. So, if you would excuse me.

730831412.text: No! Not at all! I would never go against the sage's restrictions! I just want to...

730831413.text: Wait a minute, both of you are all covered in dirt, and you're holding a suspicious stone slate... Did you just return from the desert, by any chance?

730831414.text: Are the... changes in the Mausoleum of King Deshret... linked to you?

subQuests.subQuestName: Defeat the "big guy with evil intentions"
Return to Aaru Village and talk to Soheil

730831029.text: Still, Paimon thinks that those three dots of light on the stone slate include places we have been to. Their symbols have lit up too.

730831030.text: Awesome! Just thinking about going to three separate places made Paimon tired, but it looks like we only have to find two more devices. Paimon is so grateful to Past-Paimon, hehe!

730831032.text: #Right, thank you, {NICKNAME}! Let's go look for the remaining devices!
